title: docs: reconcile Vast replacements and DreamShaper capacity regression
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Records Z-Image 52731560 and DreamShaper 52741049 promotions, retirement of 51212460/47789794, and five production-labeled GPUs with no retained retired storage.
- Updates fleet burn to $1.060148/hour ($763.31/720h); DreamShaper costs $100.27/30d and saves $8.93/month. Model prices, fallbacks, and secrets are unchanged.
- Flags an unresolved DreamShaper regression: corrected final-event queries show 0.25% 5xx before versus 4.84% after, excluding client 4xx; p95 rose from 1.268s to 2.169s. Transition also had 153 final 502s. Short windows are not load-matched.
- Documents the initial wrong model-name filter, destruction before corrected final API verification, stale-process drain hazard, and need to restore burst capacity. The isolated 210-RPM benchmark did not prove sufficient production headroom.
- Checks: named-tunnel auth/dimensions/parity/load/restart, live registry and worker attribution, corrected Tinybird final outcomes, full Vast reconciliation, and git diff --check. Biome ignores Markdown; commit hook reports missing lefthook. Documentation only; production capacity remediation remains a separate follow-up.

gist.headline: The fleet ledger blooms
gist.blurb: The hive’s GPU garden book now tracks the Z-Image and DreamShaper handoff in full, including the capacity notes needed for the next round of tending.
gist.summary: Documented the promotion of Z-Image 52731560 and DreamShaper 52741049, retirement of 51212460 and 47789794, five production-labeled GPUs, updated fleet burn of $1.060148/hour, and the measured DreamShaper capacity follow-up needed after the transition.
gist.impact: Operators now have a reconciled Vast inventory, verified final-outcome measurements, and explicit restoration targets for DreamShaper burst capacity before treating the 210-RPM benchmark as production headroom.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy infrastructure garden ledger: Polli, wearing a tiny mechanic tool belt, compares labeled GPU seed packets for Z-Image and DreamShaper beside a retro terminal and a carefully updated garden map. Small code-plants and five glowing server sprouts represent the reconciled production fleet and the capacity work still being tended.
